name: hcapp_signOutDevice
description: Cuts one device off the caller's account (E9.F7.S19). Auth: device-bound token via HC6.ValidateAppAuth (spNumber 122, @param NULL); no role needed — the UPDATE is scoped to the caller's own UserId, so a hasher can only sign out their own devices and a forged @targetDeviceId reads as not found. Revocation is the SECRET ROTATION: ValidateAppAuth resolves a device by id with no removed filter and validates the token against DeviceSecret, so minting a new secret (exactly as hcapp_authorizeDevice does) revokes that device instantly and the phone cannot re-derive it. SignedOutAt is stamped so ValidateAppAuth refuses the device with the DISTINCT errorType 7 (the client wipes the install on type 7, never on an ordinary bad-token error). FcmToken and ApnsToken are cleared because the push queries key on the token, not on removed. removed = 1 is set only so the row leaves hcapp_listDevices. A passkey on the device is deliberately NOT removed (two acts, two consequences). Wrapped by publicWeb_signOutDevice; also called by hcapp_gdprDelete.

parameters.name: deviceId
parameters.description: The calling device. Default NULL (ValidateAppAuth then fails gracefully). Recorded as 'by=' in the audit line.

parameters.name: targetDeviceId
parameters.description: The device to sign out. NULL returns 1960. Must belong to the caller and still have removed = 0, else 1961 (already signed out / not yours).

rowsets.description: Auth failure (ValidateAppAuth: 1322 device not registered / type 3, 1122 bad token / type 1, signed-out device / type 7) returns this detail rowset ALONE. The SP's own refusals return an envelope at index 0 and this detail at index 1: 1960 missing targetDeviceId (errorType 2), 1961 not found / already signed out (3), 1962 unhandled (5). No debugMessage column.

rowsets.name: ErrorEnvelope
rowsets.description: Index 0 on 1960 and 1961. NOTE the CATCH (1962) emits {success:0, errorMessage:ERROR_MESSAGE()} instead — see codeSmells.

columns.name: errorMessage
columns.description: Always NULL on success; ERROR_MESSAGE() text on the CATCH path.

rowsets.name: Devices
rowsets.description: On success: the caller's devices after the change, the same shape as hcapp_listDevices (WHERE UserId = @userId AND (removed = 0 OR PasskeyCredentialId IS NOT NULL), most recent sign-in first). The signed-out row stays listed only while it still holds a passkey.

columns.name: Label
columns.description: '<OperatingSystem or Harrier Central/Browser> on <platform>' — built from Device.OperatingSystem, IsMobile and HC6.DevicePlatformName(DeviceData).

columns.name: IsThisDevice
columns.description: 1 when the row is the calling @deviceId.

columns.name: AppVersion
columns.description: Device.Version as of the last sign-in; NULL when blank (564 rows platform-wide).

columns.name: AppBuild
columns.description: Device.BuildNumber as of the last sign-in; NULL when blank.

columns.name: HasPasskey
columns.description: 1 when Device.PasskeyCredentialId is set. The credential id and public key never leave the server.

columns.name: IsSignedOut
columns.description: 1 when Device.SignedOutAt is set — deliberately NOT from `removed`, which 300 legacy rows carry without meaning.

sideEffects: UPDATE HC.Device SET DeviceSecret = <new 75-char secret from CRYPT_GEN_RANDOM>, SignedOutAt = now, FcmToken = NULL, ApnsToken = NULL, removed = 1, updatedAt WHERE id = @targetDeviceId AND UserId = @userId AND removed = 0 — in a transaction; @@ROWCOUNT = 0 rolls back FIRST, then logs, then returns 1961.
INSERT LOG.GeneralLog ('HC6.hcapp_signOutDevice', 'Device signed out', hasher, device label, acting device).
INSERT HC.ErrorLog on 1960, 1961 and in the CATCH.
The device's passkey (PasskeyCredentialId) is left in place.

codeSmells.issue: CATCH envelope has a different shape and leaks ERROR_MESSAGE()
codeSmells.detail: Line 185 returns {success:0, errorMessage:ERROR_MESSAGE()} where every other refusal in this SP returns {success:0, errorCode, errorType} (lines 83, 128). A client that reads errorCode from rowset 0 finds nothing on the 1962 path, and the raw SQL error text goes to the phone. The detail rowset at index 1 is correct.

breakingChangeRules: Never remove a column from any rowset
Never change a sentinel value meaning
Never change errorType integer codes without updating all callers
